summary.headline: MSWIL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 47% YoY to a strong quarter, with EBITDA margin at 9.2% (up from 7.6% in Q1) despite copper and wage headwinds.
summary.overview: Management reported revenue up 47% YoY and 19% QoQ, EBITDA up 34% YoY and 45% QoQ, and PAT up 35% YoY and 54% QoQ, growing ahead of the passenger vehicle industry (volumes +25% YoY, +14% QoQ). The three Greenfield plants (Kharkhauda, Gujarat, Pune) have ramped to optimal utilisation and are now treated as part of the regular network. Copper, up about 54% YoY and 6% QoQ, is a pass-through with a roughly three-month recovery lag, and minimum wage revisions remain a cost headwind. Management guided to continued industry growth in H2 but with a narrower percentage range because of a higher base after last year's GST cut, and gave FY27 capex of about Rs 200 crore with no FY28 figure yet.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles (India)
segments.commentary: Industry PV volumes grew 25% YoY and 14% QoQ; MSWIL grew ahead of the industry on premiumisation, higher content per vehicle and new EV and ICE model launches.

segments.name: EV programmes
segments.commentary: EVs made up 10% of revenue in Q2 and 9.3% in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Greenfield plants (Kharkhauda, Gujarat, Pune)
segments.commentary: Ramp-ups progressed well; management says the three plants now run at optimal utilisation and are reported within the regular network, with no separate plant-level margins disclosed.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 demand expected to keep growing on healthy industry growth, premiumisation and new launches, but percentage growth range likely narrower than last year given the GST-cut base.
Management expects copper and wage-related price recoveries from customers over about 3 to 6 months, with better reported numbers within FY27.
No margin guidance; management said it does not guide on margins and focuses on gross margin and ROCE.
FY27 capex guided at about Rs 200 crore, largely in line with FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Can H2 FY27 revenue exceed Q2 in absolute terms, and are new programmes starting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects continued growth and ongoing programme launches, though Q3 is seasonally offset by the Shradh period and percentage growth will be narrower than last year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin decline and the improvement in other operating costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked the gross margin pressure to copper and wage costs under negotiation with customers, with recovery expected within FY27. Lower other operating costs were attributed to Greenfield revenue ramp and austerity measures; no forward guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much copper under-recovery is left if prices stay at Q2 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lag is mostly one quarter (up to six months in some cases) and that prices have not stabilised, so the residual could not be quantified; over time, it said, buy and sell prices equalise.

qa_highlights.question: Does zonal architecture reduce content per vehicle, and how much growth is at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued content growth comes from innovation and premiumisation, not only architecture, and said the harness has 7-8 million components with customer-specific designs, so full in-house supply is not feasible.

qa_highlights.question: What are the normalised gross margins versus FY24 to FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide on margins, pointing to ROCE and saying pass-through would lift the numerator and denominator together, so reported percentages may look lower even if returns are healthy.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation and FY27/FY28 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is triggered at about 80% utilisation; FY27 capex is about Rs 200 crore and FY28 is not yet quantifiable.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue growth outpaced EBITDA growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excluding copper pass-through (about 12 points of growth), revenue grew about 35% against EBITDA growth of 34%; wage impact continues, offset by cost optimisation and austerity measures.

risks_watch: Copper pass-through lag of about 3 months leaves margins exposed while prices stay volatile.
Minimum wage revisions may be only partly recovered from customers.
H2 FY27 growth faces a higher base following last year's GST cut, with a narrower growth range expected.
Gross margin dip from about 35% (FY23-25 per analyst) to 32.5% in FY26 and about 30% now (analyst figures); management did not confirm normalised level.
EV transition to zonal architecture could reduce wiring content per vehicle; management disputed this risk without quantifying it.
FY28 capex and Greenfield margin profile remain unquantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and ramp-ups, but cautious and often evasive on margins, copper recovery timing and FY28 capex, repeatedly declining to quantify them.

Normally, we don't guide on the margins. We always talk about gross.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three Greenfield plants (Kharkhauda, Gujarat, Pune) are now at optimal utilisation with no new plant named; FY28 capex is unquantified and depends on customer schedules, so new capacity timing is unclear.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: PV industry volumes grew 25% YoY and 14% QoQ and MSWIL grew faster on premiumisation and new EV/ICE launches; management guided to continued H2 industry-linked growth but with a narrower percentage range against a higher GST-cut base.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is held at about Rs 200 crore and the policy triggers expansion at about 80% utilisation, but utilisation level was not disclosed (only 'optimal'), and FY28 capex is not yet quantified.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided only to narrower H2 percentage growth against a higher base and gave no numeric revenue guidance, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Copper runs about 3-month pass-through lag (some up to 6 months) and prices have not stabilised, and wage recovery is still under negotiation, so the Q3 seasonal offset and narrower H2 growth could pressure margins.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited ongoing programme launches and new EV and ICE model launches driving premiumisation and higher content per vehicle, though no specific product was named.

rows.label: Copper and wage cost pass-through recovery
rows.why: Management expects copper and wage price recoveries from customers over about 3 to 6 months, though OEMs have not agreed to one-month copper lags and wage recovery is still under negotiation with no split given.

rows.label: Other operating cost reduction from Greenfield ramp and austerity
rows.why: Other operating costs fell in Q2, attributed to Greenfield revenue ramp and austerity measures, but no forward guidance was given and wage impact continues.

rows.label: EV share of revenue
rows.why: EVs were 10% of revenue in Q2 and 9.3% in H1 FY27, with new EV programmes launching, though no target share was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, Greenfield ramp-ups and programme launches but cautious and often evasive on gross margin, copper recovery timing, and FY28 capex; analysts pushed on margin normalisation, copper under-recovery, and zonal architecture risk to content per vehicle.
